data.name: Bheesham
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Bheesham is the god of calamity, misfortune, and affliction. He is also known as Shani, the lord of Saturday and the son of Surya, the sun god. Bheesham is believed to test individuals' resolve and discipline, and those who please him are rewarded with prosperity and success.

data.cultural_impact: Bheesham is an important deity in Hindu mythology, and his name evokes a deep sense of reverence and awe. He is mentioned in numerous Hindu scriptures and Puranas, and he plays a significant role in various mythological stories. Worship of Bheesham is particularly popular in India and Nepal, where he is believed to bring both suffering and blessings. People observe various rituals and practices to appease him, and they often seek his blessings before embarking on important endeavors.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Bheesham is seen as a teacher who tests individuals' resolve and discipline. He forces individuals to confront their weaknesses and impurities, and helps them purify their souls. He is also believed to grant boons to those who have true devotion and faith in him. The worship of Bheesham is therefore seen as a means of spiritual growth and self-realization. It is a reminder that even in the face of adversity and suffering, one can find strength and inner peace.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Bheeshma was a great warrior and the grandsire of the Pandavas in Mahabharata. The name Bheesham carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
